messages:
jess: Heads-up — hitting a weird authz gap. Customer reported embeddings API key being accepted on the /v1/chat route and returning chat completions. Not a deliberate change, right?
ryan: whoa. any repro or logs?
jess: repro attached, short curl: `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-emb-xyz" https://api.redwood/run/v1/chat -d "{\"messages\":[{\"role\":\"user\",\"content\":\"hi\"}]}"` -> 200 and chat response
elaine: that key should be scope:embeddings only. logs show it routed to chat-v2 instance though. grabbing audit id now.
infra-bot: Deploy event: rotate/kms/2024-12-03T11:34Z applied to keyring `projects/redwood/locations/us/keyRings/core/keys/rt-01`
elaine: audit-log-id az-76823. Look at authz middleware: matcher for per-route scopes uses KMS-wrapped metadata (scope list) for keys; after rotation metadata lookup returned empty for a short window and fallback allowed route-level default?
ryan: fallback allowed? I thought we fail-closed. Which commit changed fallback behavior?
jess: recent RBAC refactor (PR #4021) changed route fallback to check cached legacy-scopes if KMS metadata missing. It was intended for graceful migration but looks risky.
security-oncall: tagging this P0. impact: customer data exposure surface: low (single customer), but principle-of-least-privilege violated. Mitigation: disable legacy-scope fallback and apply hotfix. Who can prod a rollback?
infra-bot: Canary alert: 2024-12-03T11:34Z rotation triggered key metadata re-encryption. 2m window where metadata endpoints returned 500.
ryan: ok. Hotfix plan: (1) patch authz to fail-closed when KMS metadata lookup errors (2) invalidate any route-level legacy cache entries that were created in the window (3) rotate any keys that might have stale claims.
elaine: I can ship the authz patch, but need a short maintenance window to flip the flag safely. Not prescriptive huge rollout — do canary then global.
jess: meanwhile I already revoked the specific sk-emb-xyz token from the token-store and flagged the customer's workspace for manual review. revocation id rv-9921.
security-oncall: Good. Also file an audit ticket to list all keys that had KMS operations between 11:33 and 11:37 UTC. We need to check for any other scope drift.
ryan: quick query I ran: `SELECT key_id FROM key_ops WHERE op_time BETWEEN 1716822800 AND 1716823000` returned 5 key_ids. Sharing ids in #incidents.
elaine: patch PR: `authz: fail_on_kms_meta_error` ready, testing in canary. snippet: ```json
{"authz": {"fail_on_kms_meta_error": true}}
```
jess: after we merge canary, add a short-lived routing rule to reject any request where token scope == embeddings and route == /v1/chat until we're confident. Safer to block than allow.
security-oncall: Agreed. Also update audit pipeline to surface scope mismatches: if token scope != route type then raise high-severity alert.
infra-bot: Rule applied to canary: route-block-emb-to-chat (id rb-304) -> active
ryan: test results from canary: no false positives after 15m, authz patch returns 403 for any token with missing KMS metadata.
jess: rolling to global now. will monitor audit stream.
elaine: after global, we should add migration docs for RBAC refactor explaining the legacy-scope fallback and why it's being retired. Also add unit tests to simulate KMS transient failures so this doesn't regress.
security-oncall: Postmortem owner? jess + elaine. Timeline: (1) 11:34 KMS rotate triggered (2) 11:36 transient metadata errors (3) 11:38 legacy-fallback allowed embeddings->chat (4) 11:45 detection and revoke (5) 11:50 canary patch -> 12:05 global patch.
jess: opened postmortem ticket PM-512. CC: customer success for notification and offer of remediation.
ryan: follow-up action: add explicit test harness in CI to replay KMS meta 500 errors and assert fail-closed. I'll own.
elaine: also propose short-term monitoring: generate daily report of scope mismatches and KMS meta errors for 7 days post-fix.
security-oncall: Thanks team. We'll treat as SEV, but low data exposure. Keep thread updated. :white_check_mark:
